Excluding Alternative VI (the aerial busway), by 1990, the All-Bus Alternatives (VII through XI) in the Regional Core Area, would require operating subsidies of from 45 to 62 million dollars per year. Therefore, if any of the All-Bus Alternatives are selected, these subsidy requirements would severely compound the existing all-bus transit subsidy problem.
In comparison, Rail/Bus Alternatives I, II or IV would reduce the District's operating deficit in the Regional Core by a net of about 50 -60 million dollars per year; Rail/Bus Alternatives III and V would reduce this subsidy by about 33-40 million dollars per year.
F. COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Over the past fourteen months four series of community and organization meetings have been conducted to explain the program and the
results at each stage of the effort. In addition, close liaison has been maintained with the Los Angeles City Council's Transportation Committee and the Citizens Advisory Committee of the Los Angeles County Transportation Committee. Briefings have also been given to numerous newspapers and radio and television stations.
The Regional Core groups have been asked, and are expected to express their preference among the alternatives in writing to the District's Board of Directors with copies to the City Council and the Los Angeles County Transportation Commission on or before the time of the Official Public Hearings.
G. LIST OF AGENCIES
The following agencies will be asked to comment on the Alternatives Analysis/Environmental Impact Report/Statement. Other agencies, persons, groups, and organizations will be welcome to express their comments about the report as well. They may contact the Southern California Rapid Transit District to obtain copies of the draft report.
